You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

To analyze TV series popularity in this database, you’ll mainly use `TV_series` (ratings, share, viewers, weekly rank) joined to `TV_Channel` (series/channel metadata). Below are ready-to-run SQL queries for common “popularity” angles.

## 1) Most-watched episodes (by viewers)
```sql
SELECT
  s.Episode,
  s.Air_Date,
  s.Viewers_m,
  s.Rating,
  s.Share,
  s.Weekly_Rank,
  c.series_name,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  c.Country,
  c.Language
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Viewers_m IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL) DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

## 2) Best average ratings by series/channel
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  COUNT(*) AS episode_count,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
  AVG(s.Share) AS avg_share,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Rating IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.id, c.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_rating DESC;
```

## 3) Popularity over time (monthly viewers trend)
```sql
SELECT
  substr(s.Air_Date, 1, 7) AS year_month,
  c.series_name,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Air_Date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY year_month, c.series_name
ORDER BY year_month, c.series_name;
```

## 4) Top episodes by demographic (18–49 rating/share)
(Assumes values like `"1.2/4"` in `18_49_Rating_Share`.)
```sql
SELECT
  s.Episode,
  s.Air_Date,
  c.series_name,
  s."18_49_Rating_Share",
  CAST(substr(s."18_49_Rating_Share", 1, instr(s."18_49_Rating_Share", '/') - 1) AS REAL) AS demo_rating,
  CAST(substr(s."18_49_Rating_Share", instr(s."18_49_Rating_Share", '/') + 1) AS REAL) AS demo_share
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s."18_49_Rating_Share" LIKE '%/%'
ORDER BY demo_rating DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

## 5) Consistently popular: best average weekly rank (lower is better)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name,
  c.id AS channel_id,
  COUNT(*) AS episodes,
  AVG(s.Weekly_Rank) AS avg_weekly_rank,
  MIN(s.Weekly_Rank) AS best_rank
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Weekly_Rank IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY c.id, c.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_weekly_rank ASC;
```

### Quick clarification
Do you want “popularity” defined primarily by **Viewers_m**, **Rating**, **Share**, or **Weekly_Rank** (or a combined score)? And do you want results per **series** (`TV_Channel.series_name`) or per **episode**?
I want to identify the minimum share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MIN(Share) AS min_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
also want to find the maximum share of all TV series

```sql
SELECT MAX(Share) AS max_share
FROM TV_series
WHERE Share IS NOT NULL;
```
